title: Telluride Takeaways: From Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti’s ‘Debut’ to Nathan Fielder’s Audacious Dare to the Doc Branch
content:
ByClayton Davis

Chief Awards Editor

On my last morning in Telluride, halfway through breakfast at Butcher & Baker, Kenneth Branagh stopped at the table on his way to a Q&A for “Into the Breach,” the National Theatre documentary he produced. He had a story. A night earlier, he’d ridden the gondola up in pitch darkness with Willem Dafoe, Tom Hiddleston and Andrew Scott — four of the best actors alive, each with a film at the festival, sealed in one cable car with nothing to look at and nothing to do but talk. All anyone could hear was Dafoe. Branagh, laughing, called it “the wisdom of Willem.” A voice in the dark, no face attached.

I half-believed it until a few hours later, waiting out my flight at Montrose, when I ran into Hiddleston on his way back to the U.K. He told the same story, unprompted.

That’s the festival. The Telluriders have gone home, Venice wraps in a few days and we came down the mountain knowing more about this Oscar race than we did going up. Christopher Nolan’s mythological epic “The Odyssey” is still the one to beat. It won’t be a cakewalk. Here’s what else I carried down.

“The Debut” handed Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti their moment.

Jesse Eisenberg’s third feature behind the camera premiered Saturday night. By the next day, it was the hottest ticket in town. “The Debut” drops Moore’s Mona, a meek suburban homemaker who lands a bit part in a community theater musical, into the front of the best actress race. It’s the funniest, warmest thing she’s done in years. Giamatti, whom Eisenberg calls his “favorite actor,” plays the tyrant director shaping her. During one rehearsal scene between them — a master-class, no other word for it — the Telluridecrowd applauded in the middle of the movie. You rarely see that happen once at a festival. It happened again before the credits.

Moore already has an Oscar for “Still Alice,” and she’s the one to beat. Giamatti is the sentimental story coming up underneath: twice nominated for “Cinderella Man” and “The Holdovers,” never a winner and here he is doing the loosest work of his late career in a supporting turn built to be embraced. Eisenberg wrote seven songs for the fictional show. The one they’ll push is “This City May Have Chewed Me Up (But It Hasn’t Spit Me Out),” which Moore performs, and it’s headed for a best original song campaign.

Nathan Fielder attempts the impossible.

The festival’s best-kept secret came Sunday night, when ticket holders filed into the Werner Herzog Theatre with their phones locked away for “You Can See Everything,” the Elizabeth Holmes documentary Fielder co-directed with Lance Oppenheim, whose narrative feature “Primetime” premiered in Venice a day earlier. Holmes invites Fielder and his skeptical crew to film her in the 34 days before she reports to prison. The shoot spirals into a three-year descent. Portions are recreated with anA-list actor who is eligible for Oscar attention, though not SAG.

Now comes the hard part, which is the documentary branch, which has never embraced this kind of nonfiction filmmaking. Voters who prize the observational and the sincere tend to bristle at a movie where the filmmaker is this present and this implicated. The circus around Fielder guarantees the kind of coverage most nonfiction contenders would trade a lung for. Whether the branch rewards it is the whole question. Nobody has made a movie quite like this. Almost nobody has won an Oscar for one.

“Club Kid” has a real play for the old guard.

Jordan Firstman’s directorial debut had its North American premiere Friday, and its trajectory keepsgetting more serious than anyone bet on. Firstman writes, directs and stars as Peter, a washed-up New York party promoter whose life on the dance floor stops cold when the 10-year-old son he never knew about (British newcomer Reggie Absolom) turns up at his door.

Strip away the club scene and the online-comedian brand, and you have a classically built story about a man child being handed a kid. I expected that this would struggle to appeal to the older industry demographic. I was wrong. In fact, it seems to register incredibly well with older Academy voters, at least the ones I chatted with on the mountain.

Veteran actor Colleen Camp, who first came to the festival in 1977, made the case for the film’s tonal control better than any campaign deck could. “I always say, always hire somebody funny to do something dramatic, because you’ll get so many interesting things,” she said at the post-screening Q&A. “And what he [Firstman] did in this movie is even in the most dramatic moments, they’re brilliantly ironic and they’re funny.”

Firstman described how his script reversed course on him over two years of writing. “I started the script from kind of a cynical place of looking around at the scene and just not feeling good about it — looking at the excessive drug use and the sex, and being a part of it and feeling bad about myself and feeling bad about my community,” he said. “What happened was that making this film in the community — we shot at real parties, in the queer spaces in New York — my empathy really opened up in the production of the film.” That shift is on the screen, and it’s what voters will feel without necessarily being able to name it.

By the end of the panel, it came down to one word, spoken loudly by Firstman: “love.”

“La Bola Negra” commands the room.

Respect is the currency at that altitude, and Los Javis have it. Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi arrived off a Cannes run that ended with the directing prize, andthe Telluride word-of-mouth only got louder. Chris Pine, Sofia Coppola, Rian Johnson and their Netflix stablemate Danny Boyle (“Ink”) all turned up for the screening.

Shot on 35 mm and inspired by the unfinished Federico García Lorca work of the same name, “La Bola Negra” moves across 1932, 1937 and 2017, tracing three generations of gay men through nearly a century of Spanish history.

A subtitled Netflix title the festival can’t stop buzzing about is exactly where you want to be heading into the international feature race, and the streamer is hunting well beyond that category. And even though stars Guitarricadelafuente and Penélope Cruz weren’t on the mountain, the film played so well, it shows it can exist in the awards echo chamber, without them (which says a lot).

“Wild Horse Nine” made the two-stop drop look easy.

Of the titles that ran the Venice-to-Telluride relay this year, Martin McDonagh’s landed with the most confidence. Searchlight Pictures’ “Wild Horse Nine” bowed in Venice competition on Sept. 3 to a 13-minute standing ovation, the Lido’s first real roar of the fall. Two days later, it turned up as Telluride’s surprise patron screening, timed to John Malkovich’s Silver Medallion tribute.

Malkovichwas the biggest takeaway. Twice nominated and never a winner, he called the script the kind you see “every 25 years.” The double premiere vaulted him near the front of best actor, trailing only Matt Damon in “The Odyssey” and another Telluride player, Andrew Scott in “Elsinore.” Sam Rockwell, who won supporting actor for his last McDonagh outing, is back in that conversation, with the open question of whether Steve Buscemi joins him.

“Tender Loving Care” is Mike Leigh in a minor key, and it wrecks you anyway.

If this is the last Mike Leigh film, and the final shot plays like a man who knows it might be, it’s a hell of a way to leave. “Tender Loving Care” follows two social workers and was built the usual Leigh way: no script, no plot, just months of assembling people until they exist.

Marion Bailey, who plays Birdie, figured out the assignment before the assignment existed. “I could see as he was going through, he was crossing off people and I thought, what’s the sort of person he’s looking for? And then it dawned on me — he’s looking for someone who has a sense of humor,” she said. “The ones he was crossing off my list were people who don’t have a sense of humor.” Then she added the part only a Leigh veteran gets to add: “You get a call from Mike to say, ‘Do you want to come on board? I don’t know what the part will be. I’m not sure how it’ll work out, but would you like to do it?’ Yes, please. You don’t even stop to think about it.”

The film’s dedication to Dick Pope hangs over it, and longtime producer Georgina Lowe explained how the succession happened. Lucy, who came up under Pope as a camera trainee on “Meantime” and operated on “Hard Truths,” took over the cinematography after a British Society of Cinematographers function where Pope received a posthumous lifetime achievement award. “I don’t think Mike heard this, but Pat turned to Lucy and said, ‘You should shoot the next one,’” Lowe said. “Simultaneously, Mike had thought that. It just made total sense.”

Paul Jesson gave the film its thesis in a single line, asking what a movie about caring for people means right now. “It’s also a good antidote to a world which, by and large, is being run by bullies and thugs,” he said. “The state of the world at the moment is pretty terrifying, really. A lot of people try to close their eyes, cover their ears and get on with their own private lives. And it’s hard to know what to do apart from that, other than look after the people they’re close to.” That’s the movie, and the campaign.

Everybody wrote a love letter to acting this year.

Step back from the horse race and the weekend had a through-line: acting itself, in films made largely by and for the people who do it. Two of the marquee titles orbit the same building. “Elsinore” is Andrew Scott as Ian Charleson in the last year of his life, holding on long enough to play Hamlet at London’s National Theatre. “Into the Breach,” the documentary Branagh produced, tells the story of that same theater, with Judi Dench, Anthony Hopkins, Gary Oldman and Ian McKellen around a table sorting out what the stage cost them and what it gave back. One film stages a great actor’s final bow. The other rounds up living legends to explain why it mattered.

“The Debut” is the same subject from the bottom of the ladder: Moore as a suburban nobody who discovers, in a community theater musical, that performing might be the truest thing she’s ever done and nearly comes apart proving it. A drama, a doc and a comedy, all circling what it costs to disappear into someone else.

The actors branch is the largest bloc in the Academy, and nothing moves a room of performers like a film that treats performance as life or death. Telluride just handed them three.

The gondola is the place to get honest polls.

Nothing tells you how ticket holders are responding to a movie like a gondola ride to or from the Chuck Jones Theatre. On a ride up Sunday morning, you get to listen to the festival unfiltered, which, of course, came with the secret screening speculation that swung from a Frank Ocean project to the eventual Fielder documentary. But then you get to hear about people’s reactions to the Bill Gates talk at Elks Park that half the car caught the tail end of, and the running argument over which “Martin McDonagh is the real Martin McDonagh.” (Whatever that means?)

One producer I chatted with had the most useful read of the weekend on “La Bola Negra,” which he claimed everyone kept calling too long. “I felt that it was long, but I was never bored,” he said. “I was pretty engaged. It felt pretty robust the whole time.” That distinction can matter most. It’s not about whether voters check their watches, but whether they mind. Turns out they don’t.

However, he was less forgiving elsewhere about “Fjord,” Cristian Mungiu’s Romanian Palme d’Or winner. “I didn’t think there was any character work between the two of them [Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve]. I didn’t get their relationship at all,” he said. “They got these incredible actors and it didn’t just match. I wanted to hear more about their beliefs. I wanted to get more into it, be challenged more. It left me a little cold.”

Interestingly, I spoke to someone else immediately after getting off the gondola who said “Fjord” is the best thing they’ve seen this year.

The pendulum can swing rapidly between voters and titles.

Other notes from the mountain

Stephen Beresford, who wrote “Elsinore,” lost his passport and couldn’t make it to Telluride. That didn’t stop his leading man from having a moment.

Andrew Scott had company for that reaction. After the screening, Oprah Winfrey, a Telluride regular this year behind Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin’s “Everest: The Other Side,” found Scott outside and cried in his arms. If you want to know how a movie is landing on the mountain, watch for who’s weeping in the lobby or outside.

(That’s also “A Long Winter” writer and director Andrew Haigh weeping alongside them)

Winfrey also threw a party, and by the chatter, all anyone could talk about was who got the invite, who didn’t and how you could possibly get one. Spoiler alert: I wasn’t one of them.

title_zh: 特柳賴德影展重點：從朱莉安·摩爾(Julianne Moore)和保羅·吉亞瑪提(Paul Giamatti)的《首演》(Debut)到內森·菲爾德(Nathan Fielder)的膽大挑戰，再到紀錄片類別的亮點。
content_zh:
克雷頓·戴維斯(Clayton Davis)

首席獎項編輯

在我在泰盧賴德的最後一個早晨，當我在Butcher & Baker享用早餐時，肯尼斯·布蘭納(Kenneth Branagh)在前往《進入裂縫(Into the Breach)》的問答環節途中停下了桌子。他有一個故事。前一晚，他與威廉·達福(Willem Dafoe)、湯姆·希德勒斯頓(Tom Hiddleston)和安德魯·斯科特(Andrew Scott)一起在漆黑的夜晚搭乘纜車上山——四位當今最優秀的演員，每人都有電影參加這個影展，封閉在一個纜車裡，除了交談外無事可做。所有人都能聽到的只有達福的聲音。布蘭納笑著稱之為「威廉的智慧」。在黑暗中，沒有臉孔相伴。

我半信半疑，直到幾個小時後，在蒙特羅斯等候我的航班時，遇到了希德勒斯頓，他正準備返回英國。他不經提示地講述了同樣的故事。

這就是影展。泰盧賴德的觀眾已經回家，威尼斯影展幾天後將結束，我們下山時對這場奧斯卡競賽的了解比上山時多了許多。克里斯多福·諾蘭(Christopher Nolan)的神話史詩《奧德賽(The Odyssey)》仍然是最具競爭力的作品。這不會是一場輕鬆的比賽。以下是我帶下山的其他消息。

《首演(The Debut)》讓朱莉安·摩爾(Julianne Moore)和保羅·吉亞瑪提(Paul Giamatti)迎來了他們的時刻。

傑西·艾森伯格(Jesse Eisenberg)的第三部導演作品於週六晚上首映。到第二天，它成為了城裡最搶手的票。《首演》讓摩爾飾演的莫娜(Mona)——一位溫順的郊區家庭主婦，獲得了社區劇院音樂劇的小角色，進入最佳女主角的競爭。這是她多年來最搞笑、最溫暖的作品。吉亞瑪提在片中飾演的專制導演則塑造了她。在他們之間的一場排練場景中——這是一堂大師班，別無他法形容——泰盧賴德的觀眾在電影中途鼓掌。這種情況在影展上很少見。片尾前又發生了一次。

摩爾已經因《仍然愛麗絲(Still Alice)》獲得奧斯卡獎，而她是最具競爭力的候選人。吉亞瑪提則是潛在的感人故事：曾兩次提名《灰姑娘男孩(Cinderella Man)》和《留住的時光(The Holdovers)》，卻從未獲獎，而這次他在一個支持角色中展現了他晚期職業生涯中最放鬆的表現，這個角色旨在被擁抱。艾森伯格為這部虛構的音樂劇寫了七首歌曲。他們將推廣的那首是《這座城市可能把我吞噬(這座城市可能把我吞噬，但它沒有把我吐出)》，由摩爾演唱，並將參加最佳原創歌曲的競選。

內森·菲爾德(Nathan Fielder)嘗試不可能的事情。

這個影展最保密的秘密在週日晚上揭曉，當持票者進入沃納·赫爾佐格劇院時，他們的手機被鎖起來，觀看《你能看到一切(You Can See Everything)》，這部由菲爾德與蘭斯·奧本海姆(Lance Oppenheim)共同導演的伊莉莎白·霍姆斯紀錄片，奧本海姆的敘事長片《黃金時段(Primetime)》前一天在威尼斯首映。霍姆斯邀請菲爾德和他懷疑的團隊在她入獄前的34天內拍攝她。拍攝過程 spirals into a three-year descent。部分場景由一位符合奧斯卡提名資格的A-list演員重現，儘管不屬於SAG。

現在來到困難的部分，即紀錄片類別，這個類別從未接受這種非虛構的電影製作。重視觀察性和真誠的投票者往往對於導演如此明顯參與和介入的電影感到不悅。圍繞著費爾德（Fielder）的馬戲團保證了大多數非虛構競爭者願意為之付出一切的報導。這個類別是否會給予獎勵就是整個問題。沒有人拍過這樣的電影，幾乎沒有人因此獲得奧斯卡獎。

《俱樂部小子》（Club Kid）對於舊派影迷來說有真實的吸引力。

喬丹·費爾斯特曼（Jordan Firstman）的導演處女作於週五在北美首映，其發展軌跡比任何人預期的都要嚴肅。費爾斯特曼編劇、導演並主演彼得（Peter），這是一位過氣的紐約派對推廣者，當他從未知道的10歲兒子（英國新星瑞吉·阿布索隆（Reggie Absolom））出現在他家門口時，他的舞池生活戛然而止。

撇開夜店場景和網路喜劇品牌，你會發現這是一個關於一個大男孩被交給孩子的經典故事。我原本預期這會難以吸引年長的業界人群，但我錯了。事實上，這似乎在年長的奧斯卡投票者中反響極佳，至少在我與山上的那些人交談時是這樣。

資深演員科琳·坎普（Colleen Camp）於1977年首次參加該影展，她對這部電影的音調控制的論述比任何宣傳材料都要有說服力。“我總是說，永遠要雇用有趣的人來做一些戲劇性的事情，因為你會得到許多有趣的東西，”她在放映後的問答環節中說。“而他（費爾斯特曼）在這部電影中所做的，即使在最戲劇性的時刻，也都是精彩的諷刺，並且很有趣。”

費爾斯特曼描述了他的劇本在兩年的寫作過程中如何逆轉。“我一開始從一種愤世嫉俗的角度寫這個劇本，四處觀察場景，對此感到不安——看著過度的藥物使用和性行為，成為其中一部分，對自己和社區感到不滿，”他說。“發生的事情是，在社區中拍攝這部電影——我們在紐約的真實派對和酷兒空間中拍攝——我的同理心在製作過程中真正打開了。”這種轉變在螢幕上可見，這就是投票者會感受到的，而不一定能夠具體說出來的。

在小組討論結束時，費爾斯特曼大聲說出一個字：“愛。”

《黑球》（La Bola Negra）掌控了全場。

在那種高度上，尊重是最重要的貨幣，而洛斯·哈維斯（Los Javis）擁有這種尊重。哈維爾·卡爾沃（Javier Calvo）和哈維爾·安布羅西（Javier Ambrossi）剛剛結束了戛納影展的旅程，並獲得了最佳導演獎，而泰盧瑞德的口碑只會愈加響亮。克里斯·派恩（Chris Pine）、索非亞·科波拉（Sofia Coppola）、萊恩·約翰遜（Rian Johnson）及他們的Netflix夥伴丹尼·博伊爾（Danny Boyle）也都出席了放映。

《黑球》（La Bola Negra）以35毫米拍攝，靈感來自未完成的費德里科·加西亞·洛爾卡（Federico García Lorca）同名作品，跨越1932年、1937年和2017年，追溯了三代同性戀男性在近一個世紀的西班牙歷史中的故事。

一部帶有字幕的Netflix影片在影展上引發熱議，正是你在國際影片競賽中所期待的方向，而這家串流平台的目標遠不止於此。儘管明星吉他里卡·德拉豐特(Guitarricadelafuente)和佩內洛普·克魯茲(Penélope Cruz)並未出現在山上，但這部電影的表現如此出色，證明它可以在獎項的回音室中存在，沒有他們的參與（這意義重大）。

《野馬九號》（Wild Horse Nine）讓兩站的轉換看起來輕而易舉。

在今年從威尼斯到泰盧賴德的接力賽中，馬丁·麥克多納(Martin McDonagh)的作品最具自信。搜尋光影業(Searchlight Pictures)的《野馬九號》於9月3日在威尼斯競賽中首映，獲得了13分鐘的站立鼓掌，成為麗都島秋季的首個真正轟動。兩天後，它作為泰盧賴德的驚喜贊助放映出現，恰逢約翰·馬爾科維奇(John Malkovich)的銀獎紀念。

馬爾科維奇是最大的亮點。他曾兩度提名卻從未獲獎，稱這部劇本是“每25年才會出現一次”的類型。雙重首映使他在最佳男主角的競爭中名列前茅，僅次於馬特·達蒙(Matt Damon)在《奧德賽》（The Odyssey）中的表現，以及另一位泰盧賴德參賽者安德魯·史考特(Andrew Scott)在《埃爾西諾》（Elsinore）中的演出。薩姆·洛克威爾(Sam Rockwell)在上一次與麥克多納合作中獲得最佳男配角，這次也回到了這場討論中，尚不確定史蒂夫·布西密(Steve Buscemi)是否會加入他。

《溫柔的關懷》（Tender Loving Care）是邁克·李(Mike Leigh)的低調之作，卻依然讓人心碎。

如果這是邁克·李的最後一部電影，而最後一幕看起來像是一個知道這可能是最後的男人，那麼這是一種絕妙的告別方式。《溫柔的關懷》講述了兩位社會工作者的故事，按照李的慣例製作：沒有劇本，沒有情節，只是幾個月的時間來組合人們，直到他們存在。

飾演伯迪(Birdie)的瑪莉安·貝利(Marion Bailey)在任務尚未確定之前就已經明白了要求。“我可以看到他在過程中劃掉了人，我想，他在找什麼樣的人呢？然後我恍然大悟——他在找一個有幽默感的人，”她說。“他劃掉我名單上的人都是沒有幽默感的人。”然後她補充了只有李的老手才能說的話：“你會接到邁克的電話，問你是否想加入？我不知道角色會是什麼。我不確定這會怎麼發展，但你想做嗎？是的，請。你甚至不會停下來思考。”

電影對迪克·波普(Dick Pope)的致敬貫穿始終，長期製片人喬治娜·洛(Gorgina Lowe)解釋了接班的過程。露西(Lucy)在《同時》（Meantime）中作為波普的攝影實習生，並在《硬真相》（Hard Truths）中操作攝影，之後在波普獲得追授終身成就獎的英國攝影師協會活動後接手了攝影工作。“我不認為邁克聽到了這個，但帕特(Pat)轉向露西說，‘你應該拍下一部’，”洛說。“同時，邁克也這麼想。這完全合理。”

保羅·傑森(Paul Jesson)在一行字中給這部電影定下了主題，詢問現在關於關心他人的電影意味著什麼。他說：“這也是對一個大體上由惡霸和流氓主導的世界的良好解藥。當前世界的狀態實在是相當可怕。很多人試圖閉上眼睛，捂住耳朵，繼續過自己的私生活。除了照顧他們親近的人之外，真的很難知道該怎麼做。”這就是這部電影的核心，也是它的宣傳重點。

今年每個人都寫了一封致演藝的情書。

從競賽中退一步，這個週末有一個主線：演技本身，這些電影主要是由演員創作並為他們而製作的。兩部重磅影片圍繞著同一座建築。“埃爾西諾爾(Elsinore)”是安德魯·斯科特(Andrew Scott)飾演伊恩·查爾遜(Ian Charleson)，在他生命的最後一年，堅持到能在倫敦國家劇院演出《哈姆雷特》。而布蘭登·費爾德(Branagh)製作的紀錄片《進入戰壕(Into the Breach)》則講述了同一劇院的故事，朱迪·丹奇(Judi Dench)、安東尼·霍普金斯(Anthony Hopkins)、加里·奧德曼(Gary Oldman)和伊恩·麥克連(Ian McKellen)圍坐在桌子旁，討論舞台對他們的代價和回報。一部電影展現了一位偉大演員的最後鞠躬，另一部則聚集了現存的傳奇人物，解釋為什麼這一切是重要的。

《首演(The Debut)》則從底層的角度探討同一主題：摩爾(Moore)飾演一位郊區的無名小卒，在社區劇院的音樂劇中發現表演可能是她做過的最真實的事情，並幾乎因為證明這一點而崩潰。這是一部劇情片、一部紀錄片和一部喜劇，圍繞著融入他人生活的代價。

演員分支是學院中最大的集團，沒有什麼能像一部將表演視為生死的電影那樣讓表演者們感動。泰盧賴(Telluride)剛剛給了他們三部這樣的影片。

纜車是獲得真實民意的地方。

沒有什麼能像從查克·瓊斯劇院(Chuck Jones Theatre)的纜車上下來時告訴你票持有者對一部電影的反應。週日早上的上行旅程中，你可以無濾鏡地聽到這個影展的聲音，當然，這也伴隨著對秘密放映的猜測，從弗蘭克·奧申(Frank Ocean)的項目到最終的費爾德紀錄片。但隨後你會聽到人們對比爾·蓋茨(Bill Gates)在艾爾克斯公園(Elks Park)演講的反應，半輛車的乘客聽到了演講的尾聲，以及關於“馬丁·麥克多納(Martin McDonagh)是真正的馬丁·麥克多納”的持續爭論。（這到底是什麼意思？）

我和一位製片人聊天時，他對《黑球(La Bola Negra)》的評價是這個週末最有用的，他聲稱大家都說這部片子太長了。“我覺得它確實長，但我從來沒有感到無聊，”他說。“我一直很投入。整體感覺相當扎實。”這一區別可能最為重要。這不在於投票者是否查看手錶，而在於他們是否介意。結果發現，他們並不介意。

然而，他對於克里斯蒂安·夢久(Cristian Mungiu)的羅馬尼亞金棕櫚獎得主《峽灣》(Fjord)則不太寬容。他表示：「我覺得他們之間沒有任何角色的互動[塞巴斯蒂安·斯坦(Sebastian Stan)和瑞娜特·瑞斯維(Renate Reinsve)]。我完全無法理解他們的關係。這些演員都很出色，但卻沒有產生火花。我想聽更多關於他們的信念。我希望能更深入地探討，接受更多挑戰。這讓我感到有些冷漠。」

有趣的是，我在下纜車後立刻與另一位人士交談，他表示《峽灣》(Fjord)是他今年看過的最佳作品。

投票者和影片之間的動態可以迅速變化。

山上的其他消息

撰寫《埃爾西諾爾》(Elsinore)的斯蒂芬·貝雷斯福德(Stephen Beresford)遺失了護照，無法前往泰盧賴德(Telluride)。但這並沒有阻止他的主角創造精彩瞬間。

安德魯·斯科特(Andrew Scott)也有同伴陪伴他反應。放映結束後，奧普拉·溫弗瑞(Oprah Winfrey)在今年的泰盧賴德常客，參與了柴·瓦薩赫利(Chai Vasarhelyi)和吉米·陳(Jimmy Chin)的《珠穆朗瑪峰：另一面》(Everest: The Other Side)，在外面找到斯科特，並在他的懷裡哭泣。如果你想知道一部電影在山上的反響，看看誰在大廳或外面哭泣。

（那也是《漫長的冬天》(A Long Winter)的編劇和導演安德魯·海赫(Andrew Haigh)與他們一起哭泣）

溫弗瑞還舉辦了一個派對，根據聊天內容，大家談論的都是誰獲得了邀請，誰沒有，以及你怎麼可能獲得一個。劇透警告：我不是其中之一。

《綜藝》獎項巡禮：奧斯卡
